cards.rule: "No" when nothing found in his record points toward ICE; "Mostly no" when at least three times as many items point the other way. Toward enforcement: 0 votes and 0 statements or actions. Against: 6 votes and 4 statements or actions.

items.t: Voted for H.R. 1689, requiring DHS to designate Haiti for temporary protected status. Most Democrats voted yes (213–0).
Voted against the Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026 (H.R. 7744). Most Democrats voted no (4–209).
Voted against the Deporting Fraudsters Act (H.R. 1958). Most Democrats voted no (20–186).
Voted against H.Res. 1128, expressing the House's support for the Department of Homeland Security. Most Democrats voted no (9–187).
Applauded Long Beach Airport for rejecting Secretary Noem's request to play a video in the terminal; the Oversight Committee opened an investigation.
Voted against the District of Columbia Federal Immigration Compliance Act (H.R. 2056). Most Democrats voted no (11–194).
Travelled to El Salvador with three House colleagues to press the administration to return Kilmar Abrego Garcia, wrongfully deported.
Condemned ICE arrests of students Rumeysa Ozturk and Mahmoud Khalil as detentions without due process.
Reintroduced the ICE Security Reform Act (H.R. 673), which would make Homeland Security Investigations an independent agency apart from ICE.
Voted against the Laken Riley Act (S. 5). Most Democrats voted no (46–156).

cards.sum: He voted against the enforcement bills below, each time with most Democrats, and for a bill granting Haitians temporary protected status. He has introduced a bill to restructure ICE and has pressed the administration over deportations and arrests.
cards.short: Votes against enforcement bills and for TPS, with most Democrats. Has proposed restructuring ICE and pressed the administration over deportations.

cards.rule: "Mixed" when at least 3 picked votes point each way. He cast 0 on the police or tough-on-crime side and 3 against.

items.t: Voted against H.Con.Res. 96, expressing support for law enforcement officers. Most Democrats voted no (29–173).
Voted against the Cashless Bail Reporting Act (H.R. 5625). Most Democrats voted no (96–114).
Introduced H.R. 7827, the Stop Militarizing Our Streets Act of 2026.
Voted against the HALT Fentanyl Act (S. 331). Most Democrats voted yes (104–103).
Announced federal grants for Long Beach law enforcement to enhance transparency and support substance-abuse services.
With the Long Beach city prosecutor, announced a federal grant to improve law-enforcement communication systems.

cards.sum: He voted against the police-support and crime bills below, most with most Democrats, and introduced a bill to curb the militarization of local policing. As mayor and in Congress he has also announced federal grants to Long Beach law enforcement.
cards.short: Voted against the police-support and crime bills below, mostly with Democrats. Has announced federal grants for Long Beach police programs.

cards.rule: His votes decide the headline: 2 of the 6 business, finance and labor votes picked went the business way (a third or fewer is "Mostly no", two thirds or more "Mostly yes").

items.t: Voted for the Faster Labor Contracts Act (H.R. 5408). Most Democrats voted yes (210–0).

Took $290,250 from 99 corporate PACs in 2025–26, such as Amazon, Boeing, Google, Meta, UnitedHealth, Walmart and Verizon, plus accounting and law firms such as Deloitte and Akin Gump. In 2023–24 it was $26,500 from 13. Counts use each committee's FEC type, then its name.
Voted for the GENIUS Act (S. 1582), the stablecoin law. Most Democrats voted no (102–110).
Voted against the CLARITY Act (H.R. 3633), the crypto market-structure bill. Most Democrats voted no (78–134).
Voted against S.J.Res. 18, overturning the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's overdraft rule. Most Democrats voted no (0–210).
Voted against S.J.Res. 28, overturning a Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rule. Most Democrats voted no (0–211).
Cosponsored the Raise the Wage Act of 2025 (H.R. 2743).
Voted for H.J.Res. 25, overturning an IRS rule on gross proceeds reporting by brokers. Most Democrats voted no (76–132).
Cosponsored the Protecting the Right to Organize Act (H.R. 20), to make it easier to form a union.
Demanded a response from luxury retailer Loro Piana over reports of inequity for Indigenous workers.
Pressed rental car companies on overbooking.

cards.sum: He took $290,250 from 99 corporate PACs in 2025–26, up from $26,500 in 2023–24, and broke with most Democrats to vote for a crypto-friendly IRS rule rollback and the GENIUS Act. He voted against the CLARITY Act and against overturning two consumer-finance rules, and cosponsors labor and minimum-wage bills.
cards.short: Took $290,250 from corporate PACs in 2025–26, up from $26,500. Broke with most Democrats on two crypto-related votes, but sided with consumers and labor on others.
